text:
maya: Heads-up — we need owners and a quick plan for the GPU metrics we'll surface in Console for Hosted + Dedicated pools. Can we sync on what to emit and who owns onboarding?

ryan: sg. which metrics are in-scope?

maya: SM occupancy (avg/95p/99p), per-GPU mem_used_bytes + mem_total, queue_depth (pending requests), queue_age_seconds histogram, avg_latency_per_batch. Later: kv_cache_hit_rate. Labels: pool, pool_id, pool_type(hosted|dedicated), tenant_id(for dedicated), model_family or model_hash, instance_type.

sasha: +1. Prometheus names suggestion: redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy, redwood_gpu_mem_used_bytes, redwood_gpu_queue_length. Question: gauge vs histogram for occupancy? we need percentiles efficiently.

chris: occupancy -> histogram so we can derive 95/99. memory -> gauge in bytes. queue_length -> gauge. queue_age_seconds -> histogram. sampling cadence: 1s for active pools, 10s for low-traffic ones.

aj: watch cardinality on model label (hosted gets model_family, dedicated may need model_hash or omit). For tenant_id we must ensure PII-safe values (use opaque tenant_id).

maya: good call. For hosted, model_family is enough for dashboards; dedicated: tenant_id label only when explicitly allowed. Also we should emit a headroom gauge: redwood_gpu_headroom_pct to drive autoscaler and console headroom view.

telemetry-ingest-bot: New schema proposal submitted: schema_id=2026-03-gpu-telemetry-v2. Consumers listed: eng-console, eng-monitoring, billing.

ryan: one more infra nuance — SM counts differ across GPUs (A100 vs H100). Let's emit per-GPU aggregated occupancy rather than per-SM metrics to keep vendor differences simple.

sasha: add queue_age_seconds histogram so we can detect long-pending requests and backpressure. Alerting: queue_length > 100 for 5m, or median queue_age > 2s triggers on-call.

maya: action items: 1) eng-runtime to emit metrics + labels (ryan/chris). 2) eng-platform to design dashboard panels + SLOs (sasha/maya). 3) telemetry to onboard schema and rollout contract (aj). EOD Friday deadline. objections?

chris: :thumbsup: I'll start the exporter patch. will avoid free-form model names to reduce cardinality.

aj: I'll create the telemetry consumer contract and a small sample schema. will also add retention/rollup guidelines.

maya: please paste a tiny example of the Prom lines here so dashboard folks can prototype.

chris: ```
# example metrics (Prom scrape-style exposition)
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_bucket{pool="hosted-us-east-1",le="0.1"} 123
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_bucket{pool="hosted-us-east-1",le="0.5"} 456
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_sum{pool="hosted-us-east-1"} 7890
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_count{pool="hosted-us-east-1"} 150
redwood_gpu_mem_used_bytes{pool="hosted-us-east-1",gpu_id="0"} 123456789
redwood_gpu_mem_total_bytes{pool="hosted-us-east-1",gpu_id="0"} 35184372088832
redwood_gpu_queue_length{pool="hosted-us-east-1",route="/v1/completions"} 3
redwood_gpu_queue_age_seconds_bucket{pool="hosted-us-east-1",le="0.5"} 50
redwood_gpu_headroom_pct{pool="hosted-us-east-1"} 12.5
```

maya: perfect, thanks. Dashboard owners can use those exemplar series to mock panels.

ryan: retention/rollup note: keep 1s resolution for 72h, roll to 10s for 14d, 1m for 90d to balance cost.

sasha: alert suggestions noted. Also add a small 'capacity heatmap' panel that uses occupancy percentiles by pool_id.

infra-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENGPLAT-4123 (GPU telemetry onboarding + dashboard). Assignees: chris, ryan, sasha, aj, maya.

maya: wrapping up — owners = runtime: chris/ryan, platform: sasha/maya, telemetry: aj. I'll add these to the project board and ping in #eng-platform when the schema is accepted. Thanks everyone. :pray:
